independent_review.text:
# Independent common barrel V3 delta review

The V3 delta resolves the remaining V2 assertion precision issue. Each of the 21 self-scoped family injector results now passes one shared predicate requiring both `instanceof Core` and `instance.constructor === Core`. It retains public `createNgModule`, self-scoped NgModuleRef injector lookups and per-reference destruction; no Angular private metadata is read. The matching-constructor plain-object control is rejected. This is a bounded test of the intended class observation, not a claim about an adversarial runtime.

The V3 patch SHA-256 `338776e587cc23e1e524f4858bd4b821a10f586e9a062361d42aef304c7c2dc5` and manifest SHA-256 `6af86ac947bfc667654b629043c45648a0276950c62df82c4c6e3cd64fd33ee3` match, as do all 17 manifest members. Comparison of full patch sections shows only `tests/common-module/main.ts` changed from V2; all 44 product sections are identical. The patch applies cleanly to current canonical at review time. The six browser cases report all 21 family checks and missing/foreign/matching-constructor controls passing. Three individual test mutants fail at the intended missing-self, foreign-class and matching-constructor assertions respectively. Two server requests passed without browser globals. The same packed artifact SHA-256 `2828f71233d13791de86971a6d18bdc35d88d8285a9c0ed30ad624a8dff9fbe1` was used; the browser and build were not rerun by this reviewer.

The V1/V2 review of authentic tagged barrels, uniform product changes, compatibility risk from removing previously exposed names, bounded Cyph search, no CSS/HTML change, and pending Bidi/authored/metadata source-frame successors remains applicable. This evidence does not establish the full matrix, general API equivalence, admission or release readiness. No canonical files were changed.
